root_cause_proven.finding: The button regression started in 1.9.0 when app.js added named imports selectRoadtripBase and selectBaseDayTrips from roadtrip-policy.js. The previously working 1.8.8 roadtrip-policy.js does not export those names. If the service worker/browser supplies that cached 1.8.8 module while loading a newer app.js, ES-module linking fails before app.js executes, so no button handlers can be registered.
root_cause_proven.reproduction: A Node ESM test using the exact 1.8.8 roadtrip-policy.js and the new named imports fails with 'does not provide an export named'.
root_cause_proven.not_a_button_handler_bug: This occurs before initialize() and before any click/submit listener can exist.

fix: app.js now imports roadtrip-policy-1909.js, a unique module filename that has never existed in an older cache.
app.js also imports trip-model-1909.js to keep the new tripStructure model in the same clean code generation.
A one-time release-reset script unregisters old ReisSlim service workers, deletes old ReisSlim caches, and reloads exactly once.
The new service worker never falls back to stale cached JS/CSS/JSON code; current code either loads as one generation or fails rather than mixing versions.
The native app.js Start and Search handlers from the restored architecture remain unchanged.
